To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the resident-centred inspection approach is both reliable and effective for nursing homes with residents who are severely disabled and who have severe behavioural problems; the resident-centred approach is not affected by the average level of total disability or behavioural problems of the residents in the home; and the resident-centred standards are affected by the level of disability or behavioural problem of individual residents, but in a manner that is not related to the home's overall compliance.

the resident-centered process of nursing home inspection is reliable and practical, that inspectors use a wide variety of sources to assess compliance with standards and that the overall performance of homes across 31 resident-centered standards is not affected either by the average level of care needs of residents or by the number of residents exhibiting severe behavioural problems.

whether a resident-centre inspection process can be made to work in nursing homes with a high proportion of residents with severe disabilities.
the reliability and practicality of resident-centred inspection in nursing homes, rather than the validity of such inspection in terms of whether the standards are appropriate.
